literal: If one asks what virtuous action is, it is non-killing; killing will bring all other actions.
translation: If you ask what virtuous action is, it is non-killing; killing will bring about all other harmful deeds.
modern: அறச்செயல் எது என்று கேட்டால் அது கொல்லாமையே ஆகும்; உயிரைக் கொல்லுதல் மற்ற தீய செயல்கள் அனைத்தையும் கொண்டுவந்து சேர்க்கும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the essence of virtue as the practice of non-killing. The author states that if one inquires about the foremost virtuous deed, the answer is simply not taking any life. On the other hand, committing the act of killing is described as a gateway sin that brings about all other harmful and evil deeds. By upholding non-killing, a person is naturally protected from falling into other vices.
